ours.name: HRNet-W32 + probabilistic heads (v3)
ours.training: 1,161 training images (70%), ImageNet-pretrained backbone, fish-box crop input

mfld.name: MFLD-Net (retrained)
mfld.training: 1,127 training images (68%) from scratch, fish-box crop input, same split

protocol: Both models scored against our annotations on the same 247 held-out test images, in original-photo pixels, with the labelled fish box as the crop. Error figures are lower-is-better; PCK and accuracy are higher-is-better.

rows.label: Test images where the model has the lower mean keypoint error
Pass/Fault accuracy, forced decisions, 5 criteria
rows.note: Ours additionally defers uncertain cases; on the cases it decides it is 99.6% accurate (MFLD-Net has no deferral).

rows.label: Model size
rows.note: MFLD-Net is a deliberately tiny model for mobile devices.

rows.label: Inference time, one image on CPU (dev laptop)

examples_note: 8 test images drawn at random (fixed seed), not hand-picked. Green = human label, blue = ours, orange = MFLD-Net.
caveats: MFLD-Net is far smaller and faster; the accuracy gap partly reflects model size and ImageNet pretraining.
The live overlay in the app feeds both models the whole photo (the app has no fish detector), which is harder than the benchmark input.
A single uploaded photo has no ground truth, so differences on one image show disagreement, not which model is right.
